item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"They all have SCOPe 2.08 lineage class a \"All alpha proteins\" -> fold a.298 \"Left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix\" -> superfamily a.298.1 \"TAL effector-like\" -> family a.298.1.1 \"TAL (transcription activator-like) effector\", but they diverge below the family as different proteins/species: d2kq5a_ is PthA from Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri, d3v6pa_ is dHax3 from Xanthomonas, and d4cj9a_ is BurrH from Burkholderia rhizoxinica. The length spread is exactly the repeat-family issue: the SCOPe domain is made from a variable number of short TAL-like alpha-alpha repeats, so a 51-residue PthA repeat fragment from 2kq5, a 373-residue dHax3 DNA-binding repeat array from 3v6p, and a 752-residue BurrH chain from 4cj9 can carry the same family SCCS because the homologous structural unit is the repeated TAL effector module, not a fixed-length whole chain. SCOPe records the family as repeat-based with canonical representative repeat 4cj9 A:259-292 from d4cj9a_; those coordinates are representative coordinates only and must not be projected directly onto d2kq5a_ or d3v6pa_. Thus the family/superfamily assignments imply common ancestry of the TAL effector-like repeat architecture, while the fold and class levels describe the left-handed all-alpha superhelical shape more generally. Function and modeling should still be transferred repeat-by-repeat and only after aligning corresponding repeats: repeat count, RVD composition, terminal truncation, DNA target specificity, and the PthA/dHax3/BurrH protein context differ, so the long arrays are not simple length variants of one identical binding protein and the 34-residue representative repeat is not a full-domain template.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d2kq5a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d3v6pa_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d4cj9a_","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267704","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267705","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267706","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=TAL%20effector","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267609","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267596","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267589","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d2kq5a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d3v6pa_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d4cj9a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46456","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/2kq5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/3v6p","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/4cj9","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267609/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267596/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d2kq5a_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3v6pa_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d4cj9a_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d2kq5a_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d3v6pa_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d4cj9a_/parents"]}]}
